en: The Apadāna of the Elder Gaṇṭhipupphiya Sereyyavagga 9 I offered a knot-flower to the Buddha, the peerless one, the Teacher of the world, who was endowed with the ten powers. Because of that deed, I have attained the state of an Arhat; having abandoned birth and death, I have reached the end of suffering. My mind is liberated through non-clinging; I am a sage who has crossed over the flood. Having lived the holy life, I have attained final Nibbāna. This is my last birth; there will be no further existence. This is my final body; there will be no further becoming. This is my last dwelling; there will be no further rebirth. This is my last station; there will be no further transmigration. This is my last vessel; there will be no further taking up of a body. This is my last abode; there will be no further entering into a womb. This is my last house; there will be no further building of a home. This is my last chariot; there will be no further mounting of a vehicle. This is my last chariot-seat; there will be no further sitting upon a seat. “The Golden-hued Sambuddha,
Vipassī, worthy of offerings,
was preceded by his disciples.”
I went forth from the monastery.
Having seen the Best of Buddhas,
the All-Knowing One, free from craving;
With a clear mind and a joyful heart,
I offered a *gaṇṭhi* flower.
By virtue of that clarity of mind,
To the Lord of bipeds, the Tādin,
joyful with a joyful heart,
I again paid homage to the Tathāgata.
In the ninety-first aeon,
because I offered that flower,
I have not known a state of woe.
This is the fruit of worshiping the Buddha.
In the forty-first aeon,
there was a kshatriya named Caraṇa.
Endowed with the seven treasures,
a wheel-turning monarch of great power;
[possessing] the four analytical knowledges.
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Gaṇṭhipupphiya speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Gaṇṭhipupphiya, the ninth.
